intro: OBJ to USDZ converts OBJ models to USDZ on the server, with nothing to install. It is useful, for example, to bring a Blender model or a furniture and product catalogue model into augmented reality. USDZ is Apple's augmented reality format: on an iPhone or iPad it opens from Safari, Messages or Files and the model appears on the table at its real size.

OBJ is the exchange format exported by Blender, SketchUp, ZBrush and almost every 3D program. USDZ uses the Y axis up, so the OBJ model, with Z up as in 3D printing, is turned so it stands upright; the advanced options let you keep the axes. Choose the units of the OBJ and the USDZ.

The USDZ comes out as a single file with the mesh, its units in metres per unit and each face's colours, ready for Apple's Quick Look. You can apply a scale and keep the OBJ parts separate, merge them or get one per file in a ZIP.

The OBJ geometry is not simplified or repaired on its way to USDZ. Up to one million triangles are accepted without an account, two million with a free account and ten million with Pro, and up to ten files per task. Each file is converted in an isolated process on our server in the European Union and deleted when it expires.

faq.q: Why does the USDZ come out lying down?
faq.a: Because OBJ and USDZ do not use the same vertical axis. Tick or untick “Keep the original axes” in the advanced options.

faq.q: What if the OBJ has textures?
faq.a: OBJ textures are not converted: the geometry and each face's or material's colour go through.
